summary: Robert A. F. Thurman (1941–2026) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied under Geshe Wangyal, Gelek Rimpoche, V. V. Gokhale, and the 14th Dalai Lama, later holding posts at Amherst College and Columbia University.

Robert A. Orsi (born 1953) is a religious studies and history scholar. He studied at Trinity College and Yale University, later holding posts at Fordham, Indiana University Bloomington, Harvard, Northwestern, and the University of Notre Dame.
Robert Alan Goodding is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the doctoral supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert Alexander Neil (1852–1901) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the University of Aberdeen and Cambridge, and later served as University Lecturer in Sanskrit at Cambridge and Fellow of Pembroke College.
Robert B. Ekvall (1898–1983) worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Chicago, the University of Washington, and the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture.

Robert Baker Aitken (1917–2010) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Hawaiʻi, UC Berkeley, and Ryutaku-ji with multiple teachers, later working at Besant Hill School, the University of Hawaiʻi, and East-West Center.

Robert Barnett (born 1953) is a Tibetology scholar educated at the University of Cambridge. He held academic posts at Columbia University, Tibet University, SOAS University of London, and King's College London.

Robert Caesar Childers (1838–1876) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. Educated at Oxford and under Yatramulle Dhammarama, he served as Sub-Librarian at the India Office and Professor of Pali at University College London.

Robert Chalmers (1858–1938) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Oriel College, Oxford, and under T. W. Rhys Davids, he later served as president of the Royal Asiatic Society and Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge.

Robert Chambers (1737–1803) worked in Indology and law. Educated at Oxford, he was a Fellow of University College, Oxford, Vinerian Professor of English Law, Chief Justice of the Supreme Court at Fort William, and president of The Asiatic Society.

Robert Charles Zaehner (1913–1974) was a religious studies, Indology, and Iranian scholar. Educated at Oxford and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey, he served as Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics and Fellow of All Souls College, Oxford.
Robert Cummings Neville (born 1939) is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. Educated at Yale University, he held academic appointments at Yale, Fordham University, and Boston University.

Robert DeCaroli (born 1970) is an art historian and Indologist. He earned his MA and PhD at UCLA, studying under Robert L. Brown, and held posts at UCLA, Loyola Marymount University, and George Mason University.

Robert Deliège (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at the University of Oxford, he held posts at the University of Kerala, Université catholique de Louvain, and KU Leuven.
Robert Duquenne is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has been affiliated with Hōbōgirin and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.

Robert E. Buswell Jr. (born 1953) specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Educated at UC Berkeley and under Kusan Sunim, he served as Distinguished Professor of Asian Languages & Cultures at UCLA from circa 1986 to 2022.

Robert E. Harrist, Jr. is a scholar of Sinology and art history. He has held a faculty post at Columbia University, where he became Jane and Leopold Swergold Professor Emeritus of Chinese Art History.
Robert E. Morrell is a scholar of Japanology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Robert H. Brower and William H. McCullough and held an academic post at Washington University in St. Louis.

Robert E. Svoboda (born 1953) is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Oklahoma and under Aghori Vimalananda, later holding adjunct posts at Bastyr University, The Ayurvedic Institute, and the Institute for Religion and Health.
Robert Epp (born 1926) is a scholar of Japanology. He studied at Harvard University and held an academic post at the University of California, Los Angeles from circa 1967 to 1969.
